title: Emirate of Diriyah
capsule: The Emirate of Diriyah (the First Saudi State) was founded in 1744 through a political-religious alliance between Muhammad bin Saud, ruler of the Najd oasis town of Diriyah, and the Islamic reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, who preached a strict Hanbali doctrine rejecting saint veneration and Sufi practices. Under Saud ibn Abd al-Aziz (r. 1803–1814) the emirate had expanded to control most of the Arabian Peninsula and in 1806 captured Mecca and Medina, provoking an Ottoman response. The Ottoman sultan commissioned Muhammad Ali of Egypt to suppress the movement; Egyptian forces under Ibrahim Pasha besieged and razed Diriyah in September 1818, killing the last ruler Abdullah ibn Saud and ending the First Saudi State. The Al Saud dynasty later revived its political ambitions in the Second Saudi State (1824) and the modern Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (1932).
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Najd heartland of the emirate is attested by contemporary Arab chronicles and Egyptian military reports; the peripheral extent of Saudi-Wahhabi political authority across the Hejaz, Oman, and the Gulf littoral varied rapidly and is imprecisely mapped — control was often nominal or intermittent beyond the core Najdi plateau.
